bibl.title: Hagiography in the archives: real-life miracles and the sacred economy in eighth-century Egypt.
bibl.seg: Arietta Papaconstantinou, Hagiography in the archives: real-life miracles and the sacred economy in eighth-century Egypt.

Vincent Déroche, Bryan Ward-Perkins & Robert Wiśniewski (edd.), Culte des saints et littérature hagiographique. Accords et désaccords = Centre de Recherche d'Histoire et Civilisation de Byzance. Monographies. 55 (Leuven - Paris - Bristol, CT, Peeters, 2020) pp. 55-75, figg.
bibl.note: The Coptic Theban deeds of donation of children (Jeme, 8th cent.: P. K.R.U. 78-103) and their hagiographical mirrors reﬂect a common narrative self-understanding of people sharing the same textual references. But they are also building blocks in the construction of a sacred reality that reﬂected everyday social relations: they contributed to the repeated reassertion of the basic social ethics of the community.
